claims: {{canonicalName}} is a quadruped contralateral reach-and-return cycle: one hand and the opposite knee remain supported while the other arm and leg reach, return, and the other diagonal repeats.
It excludes same-side reaches, arm-only or leg-only reaches, static holds, rows, crawling, bear work, dead bugs, testing, forced range, and undeclared resistance.
Quadruped support, contralateral diagonal limb reach, a controlled return, and alternating sides are identity boundaries for this candidate.
A brief pause or declared range/tempo can be a delivery modifier only when the hand-and-knee base, diagonal reach-return, and alternating cycle are preserved.
Record trunk, hip, shoulder, wrist, knee, and contralateral support roles as task anatomy without claiming a diagnosis, isolated-muscle outcome, or clinical effect.
The task does not establish a universal limb height, spinal position, range, tissue target, readiness threshold, or therapeutic result.
One candidate repetition is a controlled diagonal reach and return from an assigned quadruped base; alternating left/right sides is recorded explicitly.
Reduce limb range, base demand, or dosage rather than accepting persistent trunk/pelvis rotation, lumbar extension, support collapse, or forced reach.
Difficulty values describe only exact exercise complexity and physical demand, never participant skill, proficiency, age, or classification.

The unloaded baseline has low external load but requires contralateral coordination, hand/knee support, shoulder/hip range, trunk organisation, and controlled return; independent calibration remains required.
Dose, effort, range, support, and context affect acute response; no universal readiness, recovery period, or performance outcome is claimed.
Track cycles per side, limb range, base width, tempo, trunk/pelvis compensation, support symptoms, and downstream work.
A clear stable floor or mat, space to enter and exit quadruped, optional knee padding or elevated hand support, and clear communication are practical safeguards.
Selection is based on the exact task and current workout inputs, not an exercise-card population or skill label.
No source establishes a universal Bird Dog dose, limb height, hold length, cadence, or readiness threshold.
Use a conservative quality-limited candidate dose and stop before pain, symptoms, unsafe support, breath holding, or persistent loss of the assigned diagonal reach-return.
Exact instructions name the hand-and-knee base, opposite arm-and-leg reach, quiet trunk/pelvis boundary, controlled return, side change, and reset.
Use a shorter reach, smaller range, wider hand/knee base, padding, or another reviewed task before forcing limb height or volume.
Appropriate instruction, supervision, environment, and progressive exposure are safeguards.
Stop for sharp or increasing pain, new neurologic/circulation/breathing/dizziness symptoms, unsafe support or surface, inability to restore quality, or participant request.

Use {{canonicalName}} only when the exact low-load quadruped contralateral control task fits objectives, logistics, fatigue, and downstream demands; it does not promise treatment, injury prevention, or transfer.
Any change to base, reach, laterality, hold, resistance, load, range, tempo, dose, or substitution reruns selection, logistics, duration, fatigue, and validation.
Athlete support should show the quadruped base, opposite arm/leg pairing, quiet trunk, controlled return, self-check, and stop prompt in plain language.
Media accessibility, exact variant match, captions, quality, and safety remain unverified until human review.

Coach support should include floor/mat and exit checks, exact diagonal pairing, front/side observation of trunk and pelvis, support tolerance, range/tempo logging, and escalation for unresolved symptoms.
Do not diagnose a stability deficit or use a generic quadruped task as an automatic substitution.

Candidate accessibility supports include knee padding, elevated hands, stable hand contact, a still sequence, captions, transcript, audio description, clear stop instructions, and a reviewed substitution when floor quadruped work is inaccessible.
These supports do not verify individual readiness or make an inaccessible base acceptable.
A brief pause, assigned reach range, base width, and tempo are modifiers only under the fixed contralateral quadruped reach-return contract.

Same-side, arm-only, leg-only, isometric, rowing, crawling, bear, dead-bug, loaded, and assessment tasks change support, action, contraction, resistance, or task boundary and require separate assessment.

Three inherited direct YouTube URLs are retained solely as unverified candidates; no playback, embedding, exact task match, captions, accessibility, quality, safety, reviewer, or approval claim is made.
Privacy-enhanced embed URLs are review artifacts only and remain non-embeddable until human verification.

assessmentSummary.identity: Bird Dog is a quadruped contralateral reach-and-return cycle. From supported hands and knees, reach one arm and the opposite leg through a comfortable active range, return under control, then repeat the other diagonal. One cycle is one controlled reach-return on each diagonal. It is not a same-side, arm-only, leg-only, static, row, crawl, bear, dead-bug, assessment, forced-range, or undeclared-resistance task.
currentCardFindings: Source 67 names the task but lacks an exact cycle, diagonal/support boundary, fatigue tracking, contextual delivery, alternate classification, calibration, and review gates.
Bird Dog ISO Hold and band-row variations already represented elsewhere materially change contraction or resistance and are not automatic progressions.
Three legacy YouTube URLs are preserved as unverified candidate media only.

proposedTaxonomy.intent: low-load quadruped contralateral trunk and limb-control practice

proposedDosage.progressWhen: the assigned base and diagonal cycle stay controlled without symptoms or compensation

coachCues: Set hands and knees on the assigned stable base
Reach one arm and the opposite leg without twisting
Make the range smaller before forcing height
athleteInstructions: Set up on hands and knees and breathe
Reach one arm and the opposite leg only as far as you can stay quiet
Return under control and switch sides
Stop before pain, pinching, or loss of support

calibrationEvidence.basis: professional core instruction, quadruped task research, legacy comparison, and inherited metadata-unverified media candidates
calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: No source establishes a unique Bird Dog score, dose, recovery period, clinical outcome, or transfer effect.

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Materialize Bird Dog as its own candidate-only quadruped contralateral reach-return definition. Treat a brief pause, assigned reach range, base width, and tempo as explicit modifiers. Keep same-side, single-limb, isometric, row, crawl, bear, dead-bug, loaded, and assessment tasks separate.
